rules.title: Agent Goal Hijack
rules.detects: both: presence probes flag a dangerous construct directly, and a control probe flags the risky behaviour when no mitigation evidence exists anywhere in the project
flags: Untrusted or dynamic content is interpolated directly into the system prompt. Anything reachable by an attacker in that string becomes an instruction.
Fetched external content appears to flow into the prompt without an intervening sanitisation or delimiting step.
The project retrieves external content into model context but shows no evidence of delimiting or marking it as untrusted data (ASI01 primary mitigation).
Zero-width or invisible Unicode character in source. Invisible to you and to code review, but a token to the model -- the standard carrier for smuggled instructions.
Unicode bidirectional override character. Source that renders one way and parses another is a Trojan Source construct (CVE-2021-42574).
Unicode tag characters present -- an invisible ASCII alphabet with no legitimate use in source. Treat as smuggled instruction text until proven otherwise.
Tool or skill description contains instruction-override language. Descriptions are passed to the model verbatim, so this is a tool-poisoning primitive.

flags: Tools are defined but no parameter schema validation is evident. Model-produced arguments should be validated server-side before execution.
No tool allowlist or per-invocation authorisation policy detected. Agents should hold the minimum tool set required for the current task.

rules.title: Identity & Privilege Abuse

Agent performs tool calls but no scoped or short-lived credential exchange is evident -- the agent may be running on a standing token.

MCP server or tool launched at an unpinned version. A compromised upstream release executes immediately with agent privileges.
MCP servers are configured but no SBOM/AIBOM, provenance verification, or dependency scanning is evident.

rules.title: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)

Shell command built by string interpolation or concatenation. Model-influenced values in a shell string are a command-injection primitive.
A code-execution tool is exposed to the agent with no evidence of sandboxing or network egress restriction.
